follow-up time: Not specified, but described as a "cross-sectional follow-up study"
cohort: 40 children diagnosed with ADHD and initiated on treatment (combined or nonpharmacological)
finding: The study found a 62.5% non-adherence rate to ADHD treatment, with social factors being the most common reason (75.7%), and caesarean delivery being a predictor of nonadherence.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was found to be a predictor of nonadherence to ADHD treatment.
